newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine firms expect no job improvement in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Argentine firms expect no job improvement in 1997.

text.p: Most of Argentina's large companies believe unemployment will stay at its current high levels in 1997, according to an opinion poll by the Argentine Industrial Union (UIA) published Monday by Clarin newspaper.
The UIA survey shows 60 percent of major companies do not expect the current 17.3 percent jobless rate to improve this year, while 17 percent believe it will rise, and 23 percent expect it to fall.
Only the construction, food and technology sectors expect to take on new staff this year, said Clarin, gaving no further details of the poll.

President Carlos Menem's Peronist government, which has promised to reduce unemployment to 12-15 percent by the time of the next twice-yearly measurement in May, says reforming labor legislation is the only way to create more jobs.

Menem is trying to push through labor "flexibilization" reforms by decree, but has met opposition not only from the unions and Congress but also from labor courts, which have declared them unconstitutional and ordered their suspension.

However, a separate poll published in El Cronista newspaper by Garcia Santas y Asociados shows 91 percent of businesses believe there will be no improvement in the unemployment rate if the labor reforms are not completed.
Among trade unionists 92 percent believe there will be no change in employment levels if the reforms are not passed -- but only eight percent believe there will be more jobs.
If the reforms are passed, 52 percent of businesses expect an improvement in employment levels while unionists believe the opposite -- 67 percent expect jobs would be lost.
